text: Fennec foxes hunt at night and shelter in burrows during the hottest daylight hours. A den can have multiple entrances.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, fennec fox fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/fennec-fox. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Beaver dams slow water and create ponds. The change in flow produces habitat used by many other species.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, beaver fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/beaver. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Monarch caterpillars feed on milkweed. A butterfly species can depend on particular host plants during its larval stage.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, North Coast and Cascades butterfly inventory; nomenclature follows the cited inventory; https://www.nps.gov/articles/butterflies-of-the-north-coast-and-cascades.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Pine white butterfly larvae use conifer needles, including those of pines, Douglas-fir, and true firs.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, North Coast and Cascades butterfly inventory; nomenclature follows the cited inventory; https://www.nps.gov/articles/butterflies-of-the-north-coast-and-cascades.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Columbia spotted frogs overwinter in unfrozen water, while local salamanders and toads use underground refuges.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, Yellowstone amphibians; https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/amphibians.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.
